children.text: by: Keilani DeSilva, Jordis Magness, Madeline Ohman

Dedication is when you commit your time, energy, and hard work towards a goal or purpose. When looking at the dedication of influencers, we look at the consistency of posting, persona, and the type of content to truly observe their dedication towards a certain cause. Across all of our influencers, dedication is displayed towards a certain cause, including relatability, religious beliefs, and helping the community. For Alix Earle, her dedication is seen in her openness and honesty about her skin and the insecurities that came along with it. This allowed for her audience to appreciate and relate to her. For Pastor Paul Drees, his dedication is shown by his use of the Bible and his constant support for those looked down on by the loud minority as he attempts to deconstruct harmful views and shows others that the Bible, at its heart, teaches the radical love of Jesus Christ. For Serena Neel, her dedication shows in her large-scale, absurd, bizarre task that ultimately helps and brings the community together while staying true to her content. Despite the clear differences among our influencers, they all emphasize a drive towards helping others before themselves. Because of their dedication to building the community, their audiences are able to connect with them through social media. Influencers' dedication matters now in the present because changing their persona or content can cause some audiences to pull back. With our influencers, they express a common theme of dedication throughout their content, thus remaining relatable and reliable for their audience and future audiences.

Serena Neel is an influencer on TikTok who makes videos of her doing incredibly random but intriguing DIY crafts and she adds a quirky, fun touch to all of her posts. She adds variety to these crafts including transformations of discarded items, unique home decor like painting her bathroom walls monthly, and many more while simultaneously structuring her content in a way where her viewers normally question what she’s doing in the comments in a positive, intriguing manner. She is such a humble influencer and many of her videos consist of her giving back or helping the community in some way but also keeping her videos true to her normal content and rarely ever shifting. She does endorsements quite regularly, but they are done in such an intelligent way to still keep the engagement coming in even though it is labeled as an ad. She usually does one-time paid partnerships with different companies with some recurring like Bloom, Cricut, and Best Buy while she also has videos not labeled as an ad but a company is tagged in her caption. Even though these types of videos are normally a paid partnership, she still does some bizarre craft or task in the video to both validate whatever product that is being promoted but also adding a crazy, fun incentive for the product to be based around in the video. This ultimately improves the credibility of the product and Serena Neel herself because viewers will see that her videos aren’t entirely based around the product because she still stays true to her core content. Serena Neel has a bubbly and bright personality, and she uses her tone to hook viewers of the for you page and her own followers to not feel the need to scroll.

Shunning others is a sign of weakness

Pastor Paul Drees is a Lutheran pastor who runs accounts on Youtube, Instagram, and Tik-Tok. His more progressive views are more alternative compared to the loudest christians, who are often pushing views that harm minorities. His style of content consists of skits where he positions himself against an opposing view that some christians hold, and then has a civil debate between the two sides. While he has a big following he remains unverified by tiktok, despite this his videos are constantly getting over 50k views and with high interactions. Paul Drees has built a brand around being a rather forward thinking Pastor, one who does not immediately condemn people with opposing views. When he acts out these skits he is even sympathetic to the opposing view, teaching them what the bible says instead of calling them bad or unchristian. His acceptance of outsiders like the LBGTQIA community has allowed him to create a community where people can come to terms with religion, and see that the bible isn't just used to spread hate.

"A bunch of caveats: there are times where someone is threatening tangible harm to others, and that is certainly a time where they can be cast out (Matthew 18:15-20). However, I often see that being invoked to cast out people who are theologically inconvenient, which is profoundly sinful. We are called to bear one another's burdens (Galatians 6:2), and lift one another up. It's a messy boundary, certainly, but one that Christians are called to walk with love. #progressiveclergy #pastorpauldrees #Lutheran #ELCA"

Alix Earle is a popular social media influencer and content creator best known for her presence on TikTok. She became widely recognized for her relatable “Get Ready With Me” videos she created while attending The University of Miami. She has gained 8.7 million followers through sharing her stories about her personal life, beauty routines, relationships, and everyday experiences. Unlike traditional celebrities who often present a carefully polished image, Earle has built her brand around authenticity and openness. She frequently discusses topics such as acne, mental health, dating, and insecurities, which allows her audience to feel connected to her on a personal level. Earle has also expanded her influence beyond TikTok by creating her own skincare line called Reale Actives, having her own breakfast at Dunkin Donuts, and joining podcasts like Therapuss with Jake Shane. Her ability to combine personal storytelling with advertising demonstrates how influencers can use social media to build a personal brand while persuading and engaging their audiences.
